children: Our Bureau New Delhi: The road transport ministry on Monday approved E100, or pure ethanol, along with E85 for flex-fuel vehicles, stepping up efforts to reduce costly fuel imports. In a notification, the ministry said E85 and E100 would be used only in vehicles designated by automakers as flex-fuel vehicles. Existing vehicles cannot be modified to run on ethanol blends higher than E20 - a mix of 20% ethanol and 80% petrol.

The government's move comes amid volatility in global oil markets due to the West Asia crisis, sharply inflating India's crude import bill. The ministry also revised certain vehicle classification thresholds, fuel specifications and technical references used in emission-related tables and testing provisions.

These include raising the vehicle weight limit to 3,500 kg from the previous 3,000 kg threshold for light petrol and diesel vehicles covered by the changes. In June, Maruti Suzuki launched India's first flex-fuel car, the Wagon R Flex Fuel, capable of running on ethanol-petrol blends ranging from E20 to E100.

Flex-fuel vehicles are designed to run on higher ethanol blends, including E85 - a mix of 85% ethanol and 15% petrol - and E100, or pure ethanol, unlike conventional petrol vehicles currently approved for lower ethanol concentrations. Major automakers, including Toyota Motor Corporation, Tata Motors and Hyundai Motor Company, are also developing flex-fuel vehicles for the Indian market. The draft amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, aim to enable wider use of fuels such as E85 and E100, as well as B100 biodiesel and hydrogen-CNG blends.

title: E100 Gets Nod for Flex-Fuel Vehicle Usage
